readerTitle: The nurse manager said yes. Why is there still no order?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (의료용품 유통업체, 검체 운송 물류 회사) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 병원에서 '예'는 한 번이 아니라 여러 번 받아야 하고, 각 사람은 같은 제안을 서로 다른 숫자로 판단한다.
misconception: 현장 담당자가 마음에 들어 하면 거래는 거의 끝난 것이다. 구매팀의 가격 반대는 할인으로 풀면 된다.

sources.text: 이 유닛의 개념 레슨: SAL-02-04 (Many decision makers), SAL-02-03 (Building a business case)
모든 사례와 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 6번 카드 계산: 연간 추가 비용 $6,000. 지난해 유효기간 만료 폐기액 $15,000의 절반 감소 = $7,500 절감. 순절감 $7,500 − $6,000 = $1,500. 간호사 시간 절약은 계산에 넣지 않음(보수적 사례).
많은 병원에 신규 제품을 검토하는 위원회가 있다는 일반적 서술만 사용했습니다. 특정 국가의 제도명이나 규정은 쓰지 않았습니다. 게시 전 표현이 과하지 않은지 확인하세요.
검체 운송 사례의 '재채혈 감소'는 가상 시나리오의 가정입니다. 실제 통계를 인용하지 않았습니다.

cards.title: The nurse manager said yes. Why is there still no order?
body: Maya runs a regional medical supply distributor. She offers a new service: her team restocks hospital supply rooms every week and rotates stock so nothing expires on the shelf.
A nurse manager at a local hospital loved the demo. "We need this," she said. Three months later, Maya has no order and no clear reason why.

image.label: A hospital supply room with half-empty shelves and a waiting delivery cart
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 병원 물품 보관실 선반 일부가 비어 있고, 문 앞에 배송 카트가 멈춰 서 있음. 벽시계와 달력으로 시간이 흘렀음을 표현. 실제 브랜드나 로고 없음.

cards.title: What should Maya do next?
body: The nurse manager is still enthusiastic. But she says purchasing "has to look at it." Maya has one more meeting with her this week.

options.text: Send purchasing a 10% discount to speed things up
options.feedback: It gives away margin before Maya knows what purchasing actually objects to. The delay may have nothing to do with price.

options.text: Ask the nurse manager who else must approve, and what each person worries about
options.feedback: This is **many decision makers** at work. One enthusiastic user rarely signs alone. Maya needs a map of every yes she still needs.

options.text: Go over everyone's head and email the hospital's chief executive
options.feedback: A senior sponsor can help, but skipping the people who review purchases often turns them into blockers.

cards.title: One service, four different questions.
body: The nurse manager names three more people. Each can stop the deal, and none of them cares about the demo she loved.

breakdown.label: Uses it
breakdown.detail: Will my nurses stop hunting for supplies?

breakdown.label: Signs the contract
breakdown.detail: Why is your price per box higher?

breakdown.label: Approves safety
breakdown.detail: Who enters clinical areas, and how?

breakdown.label: Owns the budget
breakdown.detail: Does this cost us more this year?

cards.callout: In a hospital, a yes from one person is the start, not the finish.

cards.title: Many decision makers
body: Big organizations spread a purchase across people with different jobs. The user feels the problem. Others carry the risk: price, safety, budget.
Maya had been selling to one person. Now she plans one conversation per role, starting with a question, not a pitch: *What would make this a safe yes for you?*
Infection control's answer is simple: trained staff, set hours, a sign-in log. Maya can agree to that in a day.
cards.softwareNote: Selling software to a hospital looks the same. Clinicians use it, IT reviews data security, and finance pays. A product that delights nurses can still stall for months in a security review nobody planned for.

cards.title: Purchasing pushes back on price.
body: The purchasing lead says Maya's supplies plus the service cost about $6,000 a year more than the current supplier. What should Maya bring to the next meeting?

options.text: A matching price, so the cost gap disappears
options.feedback: It may close this deal, but it teaches the hospital that her service is worth nothing extra, and her margin may not survive it.

options.text: A business case built on the hospital's own numbers for expired stock
options.feedback: This is **building a business case**. Purchasing compares prices; finance compares total cost. Using their own records makes the case hard to dismiss.

options.text: Letters from nurses saying how much they like the service
options.feedback: It shows real demand from users, but purchasing isn't paid to make nurses happy. Enthusiasm doesn't answer a cost question.

cards.title: The case, in the hospital's own figures.
body: Finance shares that last year the hospital threw away $15,000 of expired supplies. Maya's rotation aims to cut that in half.

breakdown.label: Extra cost
breakdown.detail: Higher price plus the restocking service

breakdown.label: Less waste
breakdown.detail: Half of last year's $15,000 in expired stock

breakdown.label: Nurse time
breakdown.detail: Left out to keep the case conservative

cards.callout: A cautious case that still saves money is easier to approve than a bold one that needs faith.
cards.softwareNote: Software sellers often do this with time saved per user. The same rule applies: use the buyer's numbers, and leave out the benefits you can't prove.

cards.title: Mapping people doesn't make hospitals fast.
body: Many hospitals send new products through a review committee that meets on a fixed schedule. No champion can skip it, and pushing too hard can cost goodwill.
A business case also creates a promise. If expired stock doesn't fall, finance will remember. Offer to measure results together after six months, and price the risk into your plan.
Expect a long sales cycle, and plan your cash around it.

cards.title: Now it's a courier for hospital lab samples.
body: You run a small logistics firm. You offer temperature-controlled pickups that get blood samples from clinics to a hospital lab twice as often. The lab director wants it. Finance, purchasing and the safety officer will join the next meeting.

options.text: A slick presentation about faster pickups and lab results
options.feedback: It speaks to the lab director, who already agrees. The other three leave without answers to their own questions.

options.text: One short case answering each role: speed for the lab, total cost for finance, temperature and handling records for safety
options.feedback: This combines **many decision makers** and a **business case**. Each person finds their own question answered in their own terms.

options.text: Your lowest possible price, to make the decision easy
options.feedback: Price answers only purchasing's question. Safety can still say no, and you've already given away your margin.

cards.title: Find every yes you need, then earn each one in its own terms.
body: Two ideas from this unit did the work here:
list: **Many decision makers:** a user's enthusiasm starts the deal; others can still stop it
**Building a business case:** answer cost objections with the buyer's own numbers, not a discount
cards.callout: **Try it today:** pick one stalled deal. Write down every person who must say yes, and the one question each of them needs answered.
